turnaround_reason: Inspire, the leader in implantable hypoglossal nerve stimulation for obstructive sleep apnea, was derated hard on fears that GLP-1 weight-loss drugs (Zepbound, Wegovy) shrink its addressable market, plus a slower-than-hoped Inspire V rollout and CMS prior-authorization friction. Revenue growth turned slightly negative TTM. The bull case: a high-quality, net-cash franchise whose GLP-1 fear is overdone and whose Inspire V ramp reaccelerates growth.
bullish_points: Genuinely high-quality business: ~86% gross margins, GAAP profitable (~15% net margin), and net cash (~$321M cash vs ~$29M debt)
Meaningful insider buying over the last 6 months (net +216k shares across 29 transactions) signaling management sees value
GLP-1 fear may be overdone: drugs raise OSA awareness and many patients remain eligible for device therapy as a later line
Inspire V cuts implant time >20% and ASC penetration expands the procedure footprint
Stock is ~37% of its 200-week MA after a violent derate; momentum improving (+20% over 30 days)
bearish_points: Revenue growth has gone slightly negative TTM (-7.6%), a real deceleration for a former hypergrowth name
Inspire V commercial rollout has been slow: center onboarding and reimbursement delays are pushing procedures right
WISeR/CMS AI-driven prior-auth pilot across six states adds administrative drag on near-term volumes
GLP-1 structural risk is real, not just sentiment, if long-term OSA resolution reduces the eligible implant pool
Options are only moderately liquid (call OI ~130), so sizing via options is harder
catalyst: Inspire V rollout reacceleration plus progressive CMS/prior-auth de-risking through 2026 and ASC expansion
catalyst_timing: Through 2026; next quarterly print for evidence of growth re-inflection
suggested_trade: Starter spot position (small-to-medium); accumulate on a growth re-inflection. LEAPS only if liquidity improves
key_risk: GLP-1 adoption structurally shrinks the OSA implant TAM faster than Inspire V and ASC expansion can offset
would_skip_if: Next print shows procedure volumes still declining with no Inspire V inflection, or management cuts full-year guidance again
